 Phony is almost here!
 The new Hulu mystery series starring Connie Britton and Sam Nivola premieres on Tuesday (October 20), and we’ve got the full episode release schedule.
 The show follows a teenager who becomes convinced that his mother has been replaced by an impostor after he survives a car accident.
 The first two episodes will be released together, followed by one new episode every Tuesday through December 1, according to Disney’s official streaming guide .
 When Do New Phony Episodes Come Out on Hulu?
 Phony will have eight episodes in its first season.
 Here’s the complete release schedule:
 – Episode 1: Tuesday, October 20
 – Episode 2: Tuesday, October 20
 – Episode 3: Tuesday, October 27
 – Episode 4: Tuesday, November 3
 – Episode 5: Tuesday, November 10
 – Episode 6: Tuesday, November 17
 – Episode 7: Tuesday, November 24
 – Episode 8 (Season Finale): Tuesday, December 1
 Phony will follow a weekly schedule after its two-episode debut.
 18 
 What Is Phony About?
 Sam plays Sonny Cooke, a high school student who wakes up in the hospital following a car accident.
 His mother Ellen, played by Connie , looks slightly different to him, but nobody else seems to notice anything unusual.
 Sonny begins to suspect that the woman living in his house might not actually be his mother. As he tries to find out what’s happening, he recruits his friends to help investigate.
 The series also explores the changing relationship between a mother and her teenage son, leaving viewers to question whether Sonny’s suspicions are justified.
 Connie and Sam previously starred in separate seasons of HBO’s The White Lotus .
 The supporting cast includes Grace Brennan , Maliq Johnson , Colter Lee , Meera Syal and Mahaela Park .
 18 
 How to Watch Phony on Hulu
 Phony premieres Tuesday, October 20, exclusively on Hulu in the United States.
 Subscribers with eligible Hulu and Disney+ bundles can also access the show through Hulu on Disney+.
 The half-hour mystery series was created by Nick Paley , who wrote the first two episodes and directed half of the season. Connie also serves as an executive producer.
 You can find the series on Hulu’s official Phony page.
